newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Sinaloa state to plant soybean this cycle.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Sinaloa state to plant soybean this cycle.

text.p: For the first time in five years, Mexico's Sinaloa state could plant up to 30,000 hectares of soybean this spring-summer cycle, an official of the state's Agriculture Ministry arm said Monday.
"We estimate it will be around 30,000 tonnes on the topside," Rodlofo Rendon, a deputy delegate to the Agriculture Ministry told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Rendon said the hectares to be planted depended largely on the amount of seed that farmers acquired.

"We have sufficient land and water to plant, but our limitation is just the amount of seed we can get our hands on," he said, adding the state had in the past achieved average yields of two tonnes per hectare.
This spring-summer cycle looks likely to be the first in five of seasons where farmers from the northwestern state of Sinaloa have planted soybeans to any degree.
White fly plagues and droughts have hit crops in the past and local authorities are looking to use more disease- and drought-resistant varieties to combat problems.
The Sinaloa Farmers Confederation (Cades) estimate even more hectares coming under soybean production this cycle, with plantings in May and harvesting starting in August.

"Around 40,000 hectares are programmed for the whole state, last year nothing was planted, apart from a minute quantity that did not amount to 100 hectares, because of problems we had with drought," said Cades analyst Ines Salazar.

But Manuel Beltran Lopez, spokesman for the Fund for the Investigation, Development of Plant Health for the Valle del Fuerte in Sinaloa told the news agency Notimex that plantings would not be so abundant.

Beltran said Sinaloa will plant 5,000 hectares of soybean this spring, which was expected to yield 10,000 tonnes of product. Beltran said specific farm zones had been pinpointed for the plantings to avoid incidences of white fly.
Mexico's only state to have consistently planted soybean in recent years has been Tamaulipas, with the country's demand needs made up through massive imports.
